blocks.text: **Linear search** is the search everyone already knows: start at the first value and check each one in turn until you find the target or run out of values. It needs nothing from the data — no order, no index — so it works on arrays, linked lists, files and streams alike.

blocks.alt: Searching 7, 3, 9, 4, 1 for 4. The checks go left to right: 7 is not it, 3 is not it, 9 is not it, 4 is — found at index 3 after four checks. Searching for 6 would check all five values and return -1.

elements.text: check each value in turn; stop at the first match
elements.originalText: check each value in turn; stop at the first match

items: If the value there is the target, **return its index** — you're done.
Otherwise move to the next index. If you run off the end, the target isn't there: **return -1**.

blocks.caption: Each value is compared with the target until one matches or the array ends.

blocks.text: If the target is first, one check: **O(1)**. If it's last or missing, n checks: **O(n)**. On average, for a target that's present, about n/2 checks — still O(n). It uses **O(1)** extra space.

blocks.alt: Best: target is first: O(1) time, O(1) space. Average and worst: O(n) time, O(1) space.

items: **Unsorted data, searched once.** Sorting first costs O(n log n) — more than the O(n) search it would speed up. Sort only when you'll search many times.
**Linked lists and streams**, which can't jump to the middle.
**Searching by a condition** — the first negative number, the first word longer than 10 letters.
**Tiny arrays.** For a few dozen values, a simple loop is as fast as anything.

blocks.text: The same loop shape answers many questions: the **last** match (scan from the end), **every** match (collect instead of returning), the **count** of matches, or the minimum and maximum. They're all one pass, O(n).

items: Check each value in turn; **stop at the first match**; return -1 if none.
**O(n)** time, **O(1)** space; works on any data, sorted or not.
Searching many times? Sort once, or build a hash set, and each search gets much cheaper.
